name: grpcxx
workload: Unary gRPC 'hello world' requests at varying client/concurrency levels (1, 10, 100 clients x 0 or 10 concurrent streams) over HTTP/2
claimed_speedup: up to ~3x higher req/s than official gRPC C++ v1.48.4 in the top-concurrency scenario (grpcxx libuv single-threaded: 452k req/s vs gRPC callback API: 152k req/s); also faster than grpc-go v1.56.2 (308k) and Rust tonic v0.10.2 (212k) in their respective best scenarios
hardware: MacBook Pro 2021, Apple M1 Max, 32GB RAM, macOS 14.2.1 (23C71)
tradeoffs: Much smaller feature set than official gRPC C++ (README claims '95% less generated code'); C++20 only; fewer language/ecosystem integrations; project is small/young so API stability and edge-case coverage are unproven.
caveats: Benchmark is the project author's own (comparing grpcxx against official gRPC, grpc-go and tonic); hardware and library versions are stated and the scenario methodology is documented across linked issues (#25, #21, PR #26), but the compiler and build flags used for the C++ builds (grpcxx and gRPC) are not stated, so per the evidence-tier rules this is capped at C rather than A/B despite otherwise detailed methodology.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos --topic grpc --language c++ --sort stars --limit 20

name: brpc
workload: Same-machine and cross-machine RPC echo workloads: QPS vs request size, QPS vs thread count, and tail-latency CDFs under 1% long-tail requests, single-server and multi-hop server topologies
claimed_speedup: brpc reaches ~2.3GB/s throughput with pooled connections and dominates gRPC (protobuf/HTTP2, release-0.11) on QPS, multi-thread scaling, and tail latency in every scenario tested; gRPC 'is near the bottom of almost every test' and its latency CDF 'goes out of control' under cross-machine load with some requests timing out. Also beats Apache Thrift 0.9.1 on cross-machine average latency and matches/beats it on single-machine throughput once request size grows.
hardware: Single machine: dual E5-2620 24 logical cores, 64GB RAM; multi-machine clusters of E5-2420/E5-2620 v3 nodes with 1GbE/10GbE NICs (exact models given in doc)
tradeoffs: Historically closely tied to Baidu's internal protocols and tooling; heavier/more complex than lightweight RPC libs; primarily documented in Chinese.
caveats: The document itself states the tests were run in 2015 and 'may not reflect the latest status of the package'; gRPC tested was an ancient pre-1.0 release (release-0_11) which is not representative of modern gRPC (post-HTTP2-optimizations, post-1.0); compiler and build flags are not stated anywhere in the doc, only CPU models, so evidence is capped at C.

name: SRPC (Sogou C++ Workflow RPC)
workload: RPC echo server QPS measured vs. client thread count (1-256 threads, 1024B requests) and vs. request size (16B-32KB, 100 client threads), same-machine single-client/single-server, comparing SOGOU srpc-std against Facebook's Thrift binary protocol implementation and Baidu/Sogou brpc protocol implementations, plus a cross-machine multi-client variant
claimed_speedup: ~2x higher QPS than 'FACEBOOK thrift-binary' at moderate concurrency (~312k vs ~144k QPS at 32 client threads), narrowing to ~1.6x at 256 threads (~310k vs ~192k QPS); similarly ~1.7x higher QPS than thrift-binary across most request sizes 16B-16KB (derived from page data, read off the README's benchmark3.png and benchmark1.png charts)
hardware: 2-chip/8-core/32-thread Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 @2.40GHz, 128GB RAM, 10 Gigabit Ethernet
tradeoffs: Numbers read off line charts (no numeric table provided), so precision is approximate; tightly coupled to the Sogou C++ Workflow async engine, adding a dependency/learning curve beyond a plain RPC library.
caveats: Project's own benchmark, so capped at C despite hardware being stated (compiler/flags are not). The chart labels the baseline 'FACEBOOK thrift-binary', which likely refers to Facebook's own Thrift binary-protocol server rather than a generic/optimized Apache Thrift build, so the comparison may not represent the best-tuned Apache Thrift setup. Values are read visually off PNG charts embedded in the README, not from a numeric table.
found_via: GitHub: gh api repos/sogou/srpc/readme (Benchmark section) + downloaded docs/images/benchmark1.png and benchmark3.png

name: rest_rpc
workload: Unspecified RPC echo/call workload; README claims a head-to-head performance comparison against gRPC and brpc was done, but no results table, numbers, or methodology are published
claimed_speedup: "far exceeds gRPC" (README: 'rest_rpc是目前最快的rpc库，具体和grpc和brpc做了性能对比测试，rest_rpc性能是最高的，远超grpc') — no quantified figure given
tradeoffs: Modern header-heavy C++ template design; smaller ecosystem/tooling than gRPC (no multi-language codegen, no official service-mesh integrations).
caveats: README asserts it was benchmarked against gRPC and brpc and is much faster, and links to tests/bench.cpp, but that file only contains rest_rpc's own unthrottled echo loop (no gRPC/brpc code, no output numbers, no hardware/compiler info) — the comparative claim is unverifiable from anything in the repo. Counted as this run's single allowed Tier-D entry given >1k stars.
